prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign VIRGO: the head and shoulders of a maiden seen from the front, hooded in a simple cloak, eyes lowered, with two tall ears of wheat crossed in front of her chest and a small star on her brow.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, mirrored ears of wheat and long leaves spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. The face is calm, simple and neutral, lips closed: no smile, no eyelashes, no make-up. The sign's nature shows only through form: neat, careful, upright lines, ordered rows of grain, everything in its place: care, modesty, patience, the harvest.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: cream, wheat gold, sage green, indigo. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
